findings.title: Google credential key is overwritten with a safeParse result object
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed data (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29). Line 97 assigns that wrapper to `key` and line 100 saves it as the credential key. The old code saved `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which is the data itself. After the first token refresh, every Google Calendar credential holds `{success:true,data:{...}}`, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) throws. This hits all Google Calendar users, not just setups with credential sharing on. Fix: use `.data` here, or have the helper return the data.

findings.title: Computed keys built from `z.string().toString()` create a single literal key, not a wildcard
findings.body: `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both evaluate to "[object Object]". So the schema is `{access_token, "[object Object]": unknown}`. A `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, which means that in sync mode `data` contains only `access_token` plus the placeholder `refresh_token`. The expiry fields (`expires_in`, `expiry_date`), which the comment says should be kept, are dropped. Callers then persist credentials with no expiry. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()`, or a `catchall`.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token "refresh_token" is injected even when sync is off
findings.body: The default runs on every path, not only in sync mode. In Office 365 Calendar, `refreshTokenResponseSchema.refresh_token` is optional (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:56), and the parsed data is spread over the stored credentials (line 264). When Microsoft omits a new refresh token, the real stored refresh token is replaced by the string "refresh_token" and saved (line 265-270). The next refresh then fails and the calendar stops working, with no visible error. Before this change, the old refresh token was kept. Apply the placeholder only in the sync branch, or skip it entirely when there is no refresh_token.

findings.title: Sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but several callers expect a different shape
findings.body: In sync mode this returns a `fetch` `Response`. Google expects a gaxios response with `.data` (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-95: `res?.data` is undefined, so `token.access_token` throws). Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data.error` (zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96, zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217). HubSpot treats the result as a token object. So with credential sharing on, refresh is broken for these apps. Only the fetch-based adapters (Zoom, Office 365, Webex, Lark) work. Normalise the return value, for example by parsing the JSON once, and adapt each caller to it.

findings.title: Credential id is sent as the user id to the sync endpoint
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` takes a userId and posts it as `calcomUserId` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11). Here `credentialId` is passed instead (the argument from line 69). The external app is therefore asked for the tokens of whichever user has an id equal to this credential's id. That could return another user's tokens, which would be stored on this credential. Pass `credential.userId`. This method only receives the id and key, so the userId needs to be threaded through.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported
findings.body: The file's imports (lines 1-20) do not include `@calcom/prisma`. The new `prisma.credential.update` call only resolves if a global `prisma` happens to exist. That global is set only for dev hot-reload caching, so in production `getClient` would throw a ReferenceError, and every Salesforce operation would reject. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes unconditionally, skips the sync path, and then ignores the new token
findings.body: Every time `SalesforceCalendarService` is constructed, it calls the Salesforce token endpoint, even when the stored token is still valid. It calls `fetch` directly instead of `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sharing never applies to Salesforce. It also uses `statusText !== "OK"` (line 86), which fails on HTTP/2 responses where statusText is empty; `response.ok` would be the reliable check. Finally, the returned `jsforce.Connection` still uses `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106), the old token, not `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

findings.title: Malformed body or undecryptable keys produce an unhandled 500
findings.body: `schema.parse` (line 31) and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` (line 57-59) throw on bad input, and nothing catches them. The parent app gets an opaque 500 instead of a 400. Use `safeParse`, and wrap the decrypt step in try/catch so it returns 400. The handler also accepts any HTTP method; it should reject everything except POST.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with `!==`
findings.body: The secret check is a plain string comparison, which is not constant-time. Consider `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, and handle the case where the header arrives as an array.

findings.title: Outgoing sync request carries no authentication
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no secret. The parent app cannot tell that the request comes from Cal.com, yet it answers with live access tokens. Consider sending `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, or a signature, in a header.

contracts.action: Google token refresh now goes through refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse
contracts.before_after: Before: the parsed data was stored. After: the safeParse wrapper is stored.
contracts.visible_effect: The Google calendar breaks after the first refresh
contracts.failure_mode: The next googleCredentialSchema.parse at line 75 throws

contracts.action: Salesforce getClient refreshes the token on every construction
contracts.equivalent_path: Other adapters refresh only when the token is expired, through refreshOAuthTokens
contracts.before_after: There is no expiry check, and the connection is built with the old access token
contracts.visible_effect: Every Salesforce call depends on a successful refresh
contracts.failure_mode: A non-OK status, a parse failure or the missing prisma import rejects this.conn

summary: The credential-sharing PR has several serious defects. Google Calendar stores the safeParse wrapper as the credential key, which breaks every Google user after the first refresh. Salesforce uses prisma without importing it and refreshes on every construction. The minimum token schema's computed keys collapse to "[object Object]", so expiry fields are stripped. A placeholder refresh_token can overwrite real Office 365 refresh tokens even with sync off. The sync branch returns a raw Response, which Google, Zoho and HubSpot cannot consume. Zoho Bigin sends the credential id as the user id. The webhook throws an unhandled 500 on bad input.
